_comment: Every binary entry the published tarball is allowed to carry, one entry per file. Consulted by check_pack_size's binary-eligibility predicate; an entry is ALLOWED only when every mechanical condition in that predicate holds, so a row here is a claim the gate re-verifies rather than a permission it grants. Path-exact by construction: no wildcards, no directory grants, and a second row for the same path is a hard failure. AUTHORITY: AI council 2026-09-08, 2 seats, unanimous, deep tier — it reopened the `binary` class that f573d628c closed 24 hours earlier. `archive` is NOT reopened and this file may never carry one: that collision supplied zero evidence about archives. ANCHOR: every condition the predicate checks reads THIS file, so a commit that edits a row and its bytes together satisfies all of them. The check that anchors these bytes to something outside this repository is `src/scripts/_lib/vendored_grammar_upstream.ts`, exercised by `tests/scripts/vendored_grammar_upstream.test.ts`; the threat boundary between the two is written out in `packed_binary_predicate.ts`'s docblock.

entries.why: The PHP grammar the code-graph engine loads. ADR-259 ships the parsers so a consumer install can build a graph with no manual step; compiled WebAssembly is the only form a grammar has, and the production loader reads these exact bytes.
The TypeScript grammar, which also serves .tsx. Same reason as the php entry.
The JavaScript grammar. Same reason as the php entry.
The Python grammar (road-to-a-map-that-draws-itself 6.1). Same reason as the php entry: the engine indexes .py files in a consumer install with no manual parser step.
The Go grammar (road-to-a-map-that-draws-itself 6.1). Same reason as the php entry: the engine indexes .go files in a consumer install with no manual parser step.
